newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Council says why reporter denied documents. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU Council says why reporter denied documents. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]

text.p: The European Union's Council of Ministers has been forced to explain why it refused to give a British journalist access to some of its documents.

The EU's Ombudsman, Jacob Soderman, said in a statement on Tuesday that the Council had finally answered the six complaints filed by journalist Tony Bunyan (corrects name and removes title of newspaper).
Carvel has asked to see Council documents on justice and home affairs matters.
"In its opinion the Council gives detailed arguments to support the case that it has dealt correctly with the journalist's requests..." the Ombudsman's office said in a statement.
Carvel has until September to comment on the Council's position, after which Soderman will decide whether he has enough information to resolve the dispute.
Carvel filed his complaints in November and December 1996 and Soderman wrote to the Council in January asking for its views.
At first the Council refused to give him any information on the grounds that it had no need to do so on justice and home affairs matters but it has now relented.
